target_platform_decision: This starting profile targets desktop browser prototypes. Review the intended devices before each run. The separate 320 CSS pixel reflow check still applies.
quality_check_decision: Semantic control parity is enabled. Declare project-specific token scales, text-expansion fixtures and reduced-motion limits before enabling those checks. Static captures do not establish runtime performance.
adoption_decision: No adoption thresholds are supplied. The project must declare adoption_gate and record its threshold decision before adoption. Review the catalogue floors before scoring; they are starting design goals, not validated usability or compliance thresholds.

dimensions.title: Typography and readability
dimensions.scope: Type roles, readable emphasis and line composition. Text meaning belongs to content; overflow belongs to text_resilience.

anchors.3: Type roles compete, reading is tiring, or emphasis obscures important information.
anchors.5: Text is readable but the scale or emphasis is uneven.
anchors.7: A coherent scale supports comfortable reading and clear text roles.
anchors.9: Type remains clear and deliberate across dense, sparse and difficult evidence states.

dimensions.title: Visual hierarchy
dimensions.scope: Attention order and prominence. Alignment belongs to layout; the main message belongs to clarity.

anchors.3: Secondary elements dominate or important information is visually buried.
anchors.5: The intended attention order is visible but competing accents interrupt it.
anchors.7: Importance and visual emphasis agree throughout the main flow.
anchors.9: Attention follows the intended decision order even in difficult states without excessive emphasis.

dimensions.title: Spacing and density
dimensions.scope: Rhythm, grouping and useful density. Grid alignment belongs to layout.

anchors.3: Crowding or wasted space makes related information difficult to compare.
anchors.5: Grouping is understandable but rhythm or density is uneven.
anchors.7: Spacing separates concepts and supports the declared working density.
anchors.9: Dense and sparse states retain an intentional rhythm without wasted space or lost grouping.

dimensions.title: Color meaning
dimensions.scope: Semantic color roles and emphasis. Measured contrast and color-only information are mechanical gates, not this score.

anchors.3: Color roles conflict or imply unsupported status or importance.
anchors.5: Roles are mostly understandable but accents are inconsistent or distracting.
anchors.7: Color has restrained, consistent roles that reinforce the content.
anchors.9: Color remains purposeful across complex states without creating unintended rankings or meanings.

dimensions.title: Iconography and imagery
dimensions.scope: Meaning, optical coherence and useful imagery. Accessible names and touch targets are separate gates.

anchors.3: Icons are ambiguous, mismatched or decorative distractions near important actions.
anchors.5: Most icons are understandable but weight or meaning is inconsistent.
anchors.7: Icons have coherent geometry and reinforce recognizable actions or concepts.
anchors.9: Icons and imagery add useful recognition while remaining coherent in every declared context.

dimensions.title: Consistency
dimensions.scope: Equivalent concepts use equivalent patterns across screens and states. Rendering defects belong to craft.

anchors.3: Equivalent actions or concepts change presentation or behavior without explanation.
anchors.5: Core patterns repeat but important exceptions remain.
anchors.7: Equivalent concepts share predictable patterns with justified exceptions.
anchors.9: Cross-screen and state patterns remain coherent even in unusual or expanded workflows.

dimensions.title: Craft and finish
dimensions.scope: Execution details, deliberate platform expression and rendering finish. Do not rescore consistency or contrast.

anchors.3: Visible rough edges, accidental alignment or unfinished details interrupt the experience.
anchors.5: The interface is serviceable but execution details remain uneven.
anchors.7: Details look deliberate and fit the declared platform conventions.
anchors.9: The interface sustains careful finish across primary, secondary and difficult states without decorative excess.

dimensions.title: Purpose and next-step clarity
dimensions.scope: Whether the screen communicates its purpose and available next step. Navigation structure belongs to wayfinding.

anchors.3: The screen's purpose or available next step is unclear.
anchors.5: The purpose is understandable after interpretation or exploration.
anchors.7: The purpose and next step are evident without unnecessary explanation.
anchors.9: Purpose and next steps remain obvious as context changes, without hiding needed qualifications.

dimensions.title: Interaction states and affordances
dimensions.scope: Discoverable controls and understandable enabled, selected, focused and pending states. State feedback belongs to feedback.

anchors.3: Controls look inert, unavailable actions look available, or selection is ambiguous.
anchors.5: Primary controls are understandable but secondary states are inconsistent.
anchors.7: Controls and their states communicate available actions and current selection.
anchors.9: All declared control states remain clear through pointer and keyboard paths without unnecessary styling differences.

dimensions.title: Theme parity
dimensions.scope: Equivalent information, tasks and emphasis across declared themes, not identical pixels. Contrast stays mechanical.

anchors.3: A declared theme loses content, actions or meaningful emphasis.
anchors.5: Tasks remain possible but one theme has noticeably weaker hierarchy or finish.
anchors.7: Declared themes preserve information and task quality with coherent emphasis.
anchors.9: Each theme feels deliberately designed while preserving equivalent semantics and interaction quality.

dimensions.title: Inclusive interaction
dimensions.scope: Evidence-backed comprehensibility and inclusive task paths beyond deterministic checks. Screenshots cannot establish screen-reader or native behavior.

anchors.3: The evidence shows an exclusionary task path or essential information that some supported users cannot obtain.
anchors.5: Core paths are understandable but inclusive alternatives or explanations need improvement.
anchors.7: Supported input and assistive paths preserve task meaning in the supplied evidence.
anchors.9: Difficult task states remain understandable across the supported inclusive paths, with no critical unresolved barrier.

dimensions.title: Responsive behavior
dimensions.scope: Adaptation quality at declared viewport targets and web zoom. Native window resizing requires separate native evidence.

anchors.3: Important information or actions become unusable at a declared size.
anchors.5: Content fits but adaptation produces awkward hierarchy, navigation or density.
anchors.7: Declared sizes preserve usable structure, context and action access.
anchors.9: Small and large declared sizes each use available space deliberately without weakening task quality.

dimensions.title: Motion and reduced motion
dimensions.scope: Purpose and continuity of motion, or deliberate static feedback. Preference and duration checks remain mechanical.

anchors.3: Motion distracts, obscures context or delays control without useful meaning.
anchors.5: Motion or static transitions work but provide uneven continuity or feedback.
anchors.7: Motion or deliberate static feedback clarifies change without delaying the task.
anchors.9: Transitions communicate change precisely and retain meaning in the evidenced reduced-motion alternative.

dimensions.title: Task flow and efficiency
dimensions.scope: Demonstrated prototype task paths, click budgets, keyboard actions and progressive disclosure. This is not human task-success measurement.

anchors.3: The core path is blocked or lacks a useful, understandable outcome.
anchors.5: The path reaches an outcome but includes avoidable steps or unnecessary repeated choices.
anchors.7: The declared path reaches the intended outcome with deliberate interaction effort.
anchors.9: Primary and difficult task paths remain short and understandable without removing consent or needed evidence.

dimensions.title: Truthful state and provenance
dimensions.scope: Known, unknown, stale and proposed information; source, scope, privacy and consent explanations. Visualization encoding belongs to data_display.

anchors.3: The design implies unsupported certainty, successful work or authority.
anchors.5: Qualifiers exist but important scope, uncertainty or consent boundaries are easy to miss.
anchors.7: State, source, limitations and authority are explicit where decisions depend on them.
anchors.9: Difficult partial, stale and denied states remain truthful without overwhelming the main decision.

dimensions.title: Information architecture and wayfinding
dimensions.scope: Location, navigation, return paths, context and discoverability of supporting help.

anchors.3: Users can lose location or cannot find a necessary destination or return path.
anchors.5: Main destinations are reachable but context or return paths are weak.
anchors.7: Location, destinations and return paths remain understandable through the main flow.
anchors.9: Deep and interrupted flows retain context and make relevant destinations and help easy to find.

dimensions.title: Feedback and state coverage
dimensions.scope: First run, empty, loading, progress, partial, denied, offline, stale and error states; perceived responsiveness. Static captures cannot establish latency.

anchors.3: Important work or failures have no understandable feedback.
anchors.5: Common states have feedback but difficult states lack a useful explanation or next step.
anchors.7: Declared states communicate what happened, what remains and available next steps.
anchors.9: Difficult and interrupted states preserve context with timely evidenced feedback and no misleading completion.

dimensions.title: Error prevention and recovery
dimensions.scope: Safe defaults, validation, cancellation, recovery, reversibility and exact consent for consequential choices.

anchors.3: A predictable mistake can cause an unclear consequence or offers no reasonable recovery.
anchors.5: Common mistakes are addressed but cancellation, consent or recovery paths remain unclear.
anchors.7: Consequential choices explain their scope and provide appropriate prevention, cancellation and recovery.
anchors.9: Difficult failure and interruption paths preserve user control without unnecessary confirmations.

dimensions.title: Content and microcopy
dimensions.scope: Specific labels, consistent terminology, instructions and actionable error text. Overall screen purpose belongs to clarity.

anchors.3: Vague, conflicting or misleading wording obstructs decisions.
anchors.5: Wording is understandable but includes avoidable jargon, repetition or weak instructions.
anchors.7: Labels and explanations are concise, specific and consistent.
anchors.9: Difficult states remain precisely explained with enough detail to act and no unnecessary text.

dimensions.title: Layout and composition
dimensions.scope: Grid, alignment, proportion and component relationships. Whitespace rhythm belongs to spacing_density.

anchors.3: Accidental alignment or proportions make relationships difficult to understand.
anchors.5: The main structure works but composition is uneven.
anchors.7: Alignment and proportions make component relationships deliberate and legible.
anchors.9: Composition remains deliberate across dense, sparse and expanded states.

dimensions.title: Data presentation
dimensions.scope: Tables, diagrams, comparisons, named metrics and visual encoding. Source certainty belongs to truthful_state.

anchors.3: Data encoding hides meaningful differences or encourages incorrect comparisons.
anchors.5: Data is readable but comparisons or explanations require unnecessary effort.
anchors.7: Encoding and labels support the comparisons required by the task.
anchors.9: Complex comparisons remain precise and understandable without false precision or unnecessary decoration.

dimensions.title: Brief-specific visual character
dimensions.scope: Deliberate expression of the brief. Do not reward novelty, imitate a reference, or penalize familiar native conventions.

anchors.3: Styling conflicts with the brief or feels accidental.
anchors.5: The styling is suitable but its choices are weakly connected to the brief.
anchors.7: Visual choices form a deliberate expression of the brief and platform.
anchors.9: A coherent identity supports the task without novelty, decoration or generic motifs displacing clarity.

dimensions.title: Text and data resilience
dimensions.scope: Long names, large sets, wrapping, truncation, text enlargement and supported localization or right-to-left layouts. Synthetic expansion is not translation testing.

anchors.3: Realistic difficult text or data makes essential information or actions unusable.
anchors.5: Common cases work but expansion, truncation or large sets weaken task comprehension.
anchors.7: Declared difficult text and data remain understandable with appropriate full-detail access.
anchors.9: Extreme supported content retains clear structure, meaning and action access without hiding important distinctions.
